summary: Zokito is an autonomous, AI-driven health monitoring platform engineered for astronauts on long-duration deep-space missions, such as lunar bases and Mars expeditions. Addressing the "Health Monitoring Software" challenge, Zokito empowers crews to independently track, evaluate, and act upon their physiological and psychological status without relying on real-time communication with flight surgeons on Earth. The platform continuously synthesizes key health indicators across four critical biological systems—cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, immunological, and behavioral/mental health—specifically targeting NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight, including space radiation, altered gravity, and isolation. Through an intuitive, color-coded visual interface and an embedded Edge AI assistant, Zokito detects early anomalies, explains clinical risks in plain language, and prescribes actionable preventive countermeasures. This solution is vital because as humanity ventures further into deep space, communication delays of up to 22 minutes make real-time Earth-based medical triage impossible, requiring crews to have autonomous, proactive, and psychologically supportive medical tools onboard.
details: Zokito operates as an offline-first, edge-computing medical companion that transforms raw biometric telemetry and daily crew check-ins into clear, actionable health insights. The system monitors vital biomarkers—including Heart Rate Variability (HRV), blood pressure, bone density loss indicators, sleep architecture, and mood logs—visualizing them through dynamic time-series charts and interactive status dashboards. When an indicator deviates from the astronaut's baseline, Zokito's local AI agent cross-references spaceflight medical protocols to recommend immediate, non-invasive countermeasures, such as targeted resistance exercise routines (ARED), circadian lighting adjustments, nutritional supplementation, or guided mindfulness protocols. To build the project, we used React, HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and JavaScript (deployed on Vercel) for a responsive, low-cognitive-load user interface, paired with Python (NumPy, Pandas, and SciPy) to generate physiologically accurate simulated spaceflight datasets and train our anomaly-detection models. What makes Zokito uniquely creative is its blend of clinical rigor and empathetic human-centered design: rather than presenting a cold, overwhelming medical terminal that could heighten crew anxiety, Zokito acts as an approachable companion ("Zokito") that uses gamified routine prompts and color-coded visual cues to keep astronauts engaged in their daily self-care. Throughout development, our team carefully considered deep-space operational constraints—specifically communication latency, limited onboard computing bandwidth, alert fatigue, and the psychological toll of confinement—ensuring the software is lightweight, self-explanatory for non-medical crew members, and capable of running 100% autonomously at the edge.
